entries.why_wrong: This blank line has no code at all — it's just visual separation between the module-level declaration and the debounce factory, so it can't be the source of the shared-timer bug.

This line only declares debounce's parameters `fn` and `delay`, which are already correctly scoped fresh on every call — the bug lives in the `timer` variable declared outside this function, not in these parameters.

Tapping here treats the returned arrow function as the point of failure, but closures don't automatically give you private state — they just capture whatever variables already exist in the surrounding scope. Since `timer` lives at module scope, every closure `debounce` returns captures that same variable; the fix is where `timer` is declared, not this closure boundary.

Blaming this line treats clearing the timeout as the mistake, but cancelling a pending timeout is exactly what a debounce should do. The real issue is that `timer` isn't private to each debounced function, so this call can end up cancelling a completely different function's scheduled run.

Reassigning `timer` here is normal, correct debounce behavior — every call needs somewhere to store its new timeout handle. The actual problem is that this 'somewhere' is a single module-level variable shared by both debounced functions instead of one declared inside `debounce` so each call gets its own.
